Findings from Round 1 review and corrections applied

1. Source-device binding model and authoritative ownership (OD-002)

Finding: Round 1 documented asset_data_source and source_device_key as related concepts but left ownership/cardinality ambiguous and allowed an interpretation with competing authority.

Alternatives evaluated: (A) asset_data_source authoritative binding entity owning immutable stable binding identity (source_device_key_id), with aliases referencing that stable identity and any separate source_device_key record only as 1:1 dependent/non-authoritative projection; (B) source_device_key authoritative stable identity entity with asset_data_source referencing it through a strictly defined relationship.

Evaluation criteria: single source of truth, cardinality, ownership/lifecycle, fingerprint alias references, multiple sources reporting one canonical asset, merge/split effects, key rotation and alias overlap, historical binding preservation, referential integrity and tenant-inclusive FK feasibility.

Recommendation (Proposed, not approved): Alternative A. asset_data_source is the authoritative stable source-device binding entity and owns immutable source_device_key_id, binding provenance, and lifecycle; source_device_fingerprint_alias references this stable binding identity; a separate source_device_key entity, if materialized, must be 1:1, same-lifecycle, dependent/non-authoritative, and contain no competing attributes. Alternative B increases dual-authority/lifecycle split risk unless exhaustively constrained.

Corrections applied: updated entity catalogue, relationship analysis (R4/R5), identity notes, ERDs (binding relationships/entities/labels), and transaction boundaries to reflect the recommended single-source-of-truth model while preserving OD-002 as an open decision requiring technical approval.

Status: Proposed / Open Decision (OD-002). No technical approval or ADR acceptance granted.

2. Identity/licensing idempotency contract (OD-008 / TD-007)

Finding: identity_operation_idempotency_ledger and transaction operations lacked a complete logical contract for key scope, canonicalization/hash, state semantics, concurrent/retry behavior, unknown-commit handling, and coupling model.

Alternatives evaluated: (A) single-transaction coupling of ledger claim/state/result with database-local business state, audit/history/licensing, and required outbox records; (B) staged/multi-transaction tracking with in_progress claims, leases/fencing, and recovery.

Recommendation (Proposed, not approved): define a durable logical contract (tenant + operation type + idempotency key scope; deterministic request canonicalization/hash; states in_progress, committed, failed_terminal, timeout_unknown_commit; replay/conflict/concurrency/unknown-commit rules; retention/reconciliation requirement). Default for database-local identity/licensing operations: Alternative A (single-transaction coupling). Staged tracking (B) only where single DB-local transaction is infeasible and explicit leases/fencing/recovery are approved. Database-local atomicity remains separate from external side effects coordinated through outbox; no exactly-once external delivery claimed.

Corrections applied: updated idempotency ledger entity definition, transaction global principles and identity/licensing operation semantics, and ERD idempotency fields/notes.

Status: Proposed / Open Decision (OD-008). Contract approval, operation scope, retention, and any staged exceptions require technical approval.

3. Event receipt deduplication namespace

Finding: event_receipt uniqueness/namespace guidance was insufficiently explicit for connectors where upstream event IDs are globally unique within a data source, unique only within a device, or unreliable/missing; this risked cross-device collisions in multi-device connectors.

Alternatives evaluated: tenant+data source namespace, tenant+stable source-device binding namespace, and explicitly modeled event namespace (type + namespace id + normalized key + provenance).

Recommendation (Proposed): use an explicitly modeled deduplication namespace/provenance on event_receipt. Data-source-global upstream IDs may use tenant+data_source_id namespace; device-scoped upstream IDs must use tenant+authoritative stable source-device binding identity namespace; unreliable/missing upstream IDs require deterministic approved fallback or reject/quarantine policy. Raw source identifiers are not DB uniqueness keys. event_receipt remains distinct from identity_operation_idempotency_ledger.

Corrections applied: updated event_receipt entity, relationship/matrix references, ERDs, and transaction operation 10 (atomic acceptance, uniqueness, concurrency, unresolved connector-specific behavior).

Status: namespace model Proposed; connector-specific fallback/unreliable-ID behavior recorded as Open Decision (OD-013) where necessary.

4. Asset lineage relational integrity

Finding: asset_lineage_link used a polymorphic generic reference (from_asset_or_op_ref) that cannot be guaranteed by a conventional relational foreign key; application-only validation is insufficient where structural integrity is possible.

Alternatives evaluated: typed source/target asset references only, explicit operation-to-lineage entities, separate merge/split lineage associations, and a single typed lineage table with nullable operation FKs by link type.

Recommendation (Proposed): adopt typed, relationally enforceable lineage associations. asset_lineage_link (or equivalent typed associations) must carry typed from_asset_id/to_asset_id FKs and typed operation FKs (merge_operation_id / split_operation_id) with link-type-valid exclusivity/constraints, preserving canonical asset identity, non-reusable IDs, merge survivor/losing history, split source/result history, tenant boundaries, auditability, and referential integrity.

Corrections applied: replaced polymorphic lineage entity/attributes in catalogue and ERD; updated merge/split transaction boundaries and lineage notes.

Status: Proposed correction documented in logical model; physical constraint syntax remains future schema design.

5. Entity naming and responsibility normalization

Findings and dispositions (Proposed, traceability preserved):

Candidate(s) Disposition Rationale
permission_assignment vs role_permission Normalized: role_permission canonical (role→capability); membership_role_assignment retained separately (membership→role); permission_assignment not separately modeled Removes ambiguous grant target; distinct RBAC responsibilities
tenant_configuration vs tenant_policy_reference Normalized: tenant_configuration canonical (includes policy/version references); tenant_policy_reference not separate competing entity Single tenant-scoped config authority
audit_event vs ai_interaction_audit Retained as separate (specialization/association via correlation, not duplicate truth) Distinct responsibilities: operational/security audit vs AI privacy/provider decision metadata (no full prompt/response by default)
asset_tombstone vs terminal asset lifecycle representation Retained as distinct optional representation (tombstone separate from mutable lifecycle state/history) Preserves non-reusable terminal-history semantics without conflating routine state transitions
processing_work_item Optional / intentionally not core; omitted from core ERDs unless justified Avoids speculative pipeline schema and competing state truth with outbox/event records
outbox_message vs outbox_attempt Retained as separate Work intent/state vs attempt/lease/ambiguity/replay history

Corrections applied: catalogue rows, ERD labels/entities/omission notes, relationship matrix entry, and classification matrix naming aligned.
